title: Ops mini-retro: latency bias scrub
content:
Purpose: quick retrospective and operational scrub after this week’s surge / latency blips. Short meeting — captured anomalies, immediate mitigations, and action items for capacity tuning and telemetry improvements.

Attendees: Priya (chair), Ethan, Liang, Ana, Sam (SRE), Maria (observability), + on-call rotation.

TL;DR: two small but correlated problems surfaced mid-week — (1) region routing bias toward cheaper replicas increased p95/p99 in EU for low-volume customers, and (2) slot preemption during a Dedicated burst caused brief queue stacking in us-west. No customer-visible SLA breach, but noise in tail latencies.

What happened (high-level):
- On 2026-05-19 10:33 UTC a cost-based routing policy (experimental) shifted ~12% of steady traffic from eu-central primary pool to eu-west cheaper variants. Those variants had slightly different kernel selections and smaller batch windows; baseline latency increased. The change was gradual but raised p95 by ~90ms and p99 by ~230ms for short-chat workloads.
- Simultaneously, a reserved-capacity burst for a single Dedicated customer in us-west triggered preemption of opportunistic backfill slots. The backfill controller reclaimed slots aggressively (config: reclaim-threshold=0.6), which caused short-lived queueing on the opportunistic lane for ~4 minutes as the autoscaler reconciled.

Metrics snapshot (baseline vs spike):
- eu-central avg token latency (short-chat): baseline 28ms -> spike 118ms
- eu-central p95: baseline 52ms -> spike 142ms
- eu-central p99: baseline 110ms -> spike 340ms
- us-west opportunistic queue length: baseline 0-2 -> spike 38
- preemption rate (us-west, 10m window): 0.4% -> 3.9%
- overall token throughput: steady at 1.02M tps (no change)

Root-cause hypotheses (open):
1) Routing bias tuning overly sensitive to short-term cost signals. The heuristics favored cheaper variants without verifying kernel or batch profile compatibility, so tail latency was impacted.
2) Backfill reclaim policy is too aggressive during bursts; reclaim-threshold and reconciliation delay knobs insufficiently smoothed.
3) Telemetry missing a quick comparator between routing decision and per-variant performance profile (we lack an end-to-end pre-eval check).

Immediate mitigations performed (during incident/week):
- Rolled back experimental cost-signal weight to 0. Drop restored to previous stable routing policy at 10:51 UTC.
- Temporarily increased backfill reconciliation delay from 15s -> 45s to smooth reclaim ripples.
- Pinned critical low-latency customers to eu-central primary pool until we complete evaluation.

Notes from the scrub:
- Liang: observed kernel mismatch (quantized matmul path) on cheaper eu-west variant that increases per-token CPU in the mixing path. Need per-variant kernel compatibility metadata surfaced to router.
- Maria: gaps found in dashboards — we do not publish per-routing-decision latency deltas. Suggest adding a lightweight delta metric that logs (route_decision_id, delta_p95) sampled 1/1000 requests.
- Ethan: backfill controller should implement a soft reclaim window (exponential backoff) for the first 2 minutes after a reclaim storm is detected.

Action items (owner — ETA):
- Add kernel-compat flags to model catalog entries and make router consult them before migrating traffic. (Liang — 2026-05-28)
- Implement sampled route-decision delta metric and dashboard to show p50/p95 before vs after routing changes. (Maria + Observability — 2026-06-04)
- Backfill controller: introduce soft reclaim/backoff + configurable reclaim-threshold per region; start with us-west. (Ethan — prototype 2026-05-27)
- Run a controlled canary of cost-routing using synthetic traffic with the new telemetry to detect negative deltas before rollouts. (Priya — plan 2026-05-25; canary 2026-05-29)
- Update runbook snippet for immediate rollback steps and who to page for routing-policy rollbacks. (Sam — 2026-05-23)
- Short-term: create a per-customer pinning API to lock critical customers to a chosen pool until median p95 delta < 30ms for 24h. (Ana — 2026-05-26)

Design notes / tradeoffs discussed:
- We accept small cost variance to preserve latency SLOs for low-latency customers. The panel agreed to reduce aggressive cost-seeking in the router unless the variant provides a previously validated performance profile.
- Longer reclaim windows reduce capacity agility for true bursts; we should differentiate reclaim behavior between "guaranteed" and "opportunistic" clients. That suggests an extended policy matrix but increases complexity. Proposal: add a soft budget where opportunistic slots may be reclaimed only up to X% in a 5m window unless explicit emergency flag.

Telemetry + observability backlog (short):
- Per-variant kernel tag in model-catalog (metadata).
- Route-decision delta metric (sampled).
- Per-region slot occupancy heatmap (1m granularity).
- Add an alert rule: sustained p95 delta > 75ms for >5m after routing policy change -> auto-rollback trigger (manual approve window).

Followups for next week:
- Liang and Maria to run a small lab: replay week-of-traffic from May 12-19 against the cheaper variant perf profiles and capture deltas. Deliver a one-pager with recommendations. (due 2026-05-28)
- Ethan to wire a backfill soft-reclaim prototype in staging and run a 48h soak with synthetic reclaim storms. (ready 2026-05-27)
- Priya to run the canary with the new telemetry and convene a short post-canary review (~1 hour) if any delta > 50ms is observed. (canary 2026-05-29)

Open questions / risks:
- How many variants lack kernel-compat metadata? Quick scan suggests ~18% of the catalog may be missing tags — this could slow rollout.
- Does per-customer pinning materially increase operational complexity for sales/CS? We need a simple UI and api.
- Is the autoscaler reconciling fast enough for real-time Dedicated bursts? Might need to tune reserved capacity pre-warm thresholds.

Meeting notes (freeform):
- Ana suggested a small "safety net" lane — keep a small pool of warm slots per region reserved for p95-sensitive customers. This is similar to reserved tenants but cheaper (opportunistic reservations). Worth prototyping.
- Sam reminded team to add short-circuit runbook steps that allow on-call to lower routing-cost weight to 0 with a single command.
- Maria: will add temporary synthetic checks that exercise route decision and check for per-variant perf mismatches.

Appendix — quick checklist for on-call (to add to runbook):
- If p95 spikes after routing change: 1) immediately set routing-cost-weight=0, 2) pin critical customers, 3) notify infra-leads, 4) open triage ticket INFRA-XXXX, 5) monitor delta metric.
- If queue stacking due to preemption: 1) increase backfill-reconciliation-delay to 45s, 2) temporarily reduce reclaim-threshold by 10%, 3) trigger backfill-storm analysis job.

Closing: overall the system behaved gracefully — automated rollbacks and the on-call playbook prevented customer impact. The main gaps are in pre-deployment validation of variant performance and more nuanced reclaim policies. Next week focus is telemetry + backfill soft-reclaim prototype.

Notes-to-self (Priya): follow up with Product on whether pinning API needs billing changes; loop in CS for customer pinning UX.

-- end --
